Job Description

This Opportunity

WSP is initiating a search for a Senior Project Coordinator – CenterPoint Energy Portfolio based in the Houston, Texas area to join our Power & Energy team.

This role will provide project coordination and delivery support across a portfolio of approximately four to six concurrent project teams. The successful candidate will work closely with project managers, project controls personnel, technical leads, commercial teams, and client stakeholders to maintain organized, accurate, and timely project information.

The Senior Project Coordinator will independently coordinate project meetings, action items, deliverables, documentation, reporting cycles, and administrative workflows across multiple projects. This person must be comfortable working in a fast-paced, client-facing environment, anticipating team needs, following assignments through completion, and escalating schedule, documentation, commercial, or compliance concerns when appropriate.

This position requires regular in-person support in the Houston area, including attendance at project meetings, workshops, client offices, and other project locations as business needs require. The role is not intended to be performed exclusively remotely.

Your Impact

The current list is comprehensive, but it contains some overlapping or generalized duties. I recommend organizing it around the actual project delivery functions you need this person to perform.

Project and portfolio coordination

Provide consistent coordination support across four to six concurrent project teams, adjusting priorities as project needs and deadlines change.
Maintain project coordination plans, deliverable registers, action-item logs, decision logs, risk and issue logs, change or trend logs, and other project control records as assigned.
Track commitments, upcoming milestones, required inputs, and due dates; proactively follow up with responsible team members and escalate potential delays.
Help project managers maintain consistent project governance, reporting, documentation, and communication practices across the portfolio.
Coordinate activities among project managers, project controls, technical disciplines, commercial teams, subcontractors, and client stakeholders.

Meetings and communication

Coordinate recurring project meetings, workshops, client reviews, and working sessions, including scheduling, agenda preparation, meeting materials, notes, decisions, and action-item tracking.
Produce concise and accurate meeting records that clearly identify assignments, responsible parties, required dates, decisions, and unresolved items.
Follow action items through closure rather than limiting support to meeting-note preparation and distribution.
Draft routine project correspondence, status updates, requests for information, and follow-up communications for project manager review.
Maintain professional and responsive communication with internal and external stakeholders.

Deliverables and document control

Coordinate the planning, preparation, internal review, quality review, client submission, comment resolution, and finalization of project deliverables.
Maintain deliverable registers and production schedules showing responsible contributors, planned review dates, submission dates, and current status.
Administer project documentation, including contracts, scopes of work, submittals, RFIs, change documentation, technical deliverables, correspondence, and approvals.
Maintain organized project files and repositories using established naming, version-control, access, retention, and audit requirements.
Verify that current and approved versions of project information are accessible to appropriate team members.

Project controls and reporting

Coordinate recurring project reporting cycles and collect inputs from project managers, schedulers, cost personnel, and technical leads.
Support the maintenance of dashboards, milestone reports, KPI reports, cost reports, schedule updates, risk registers, and change-management records.
Review project information for completeness, internal consistency, and data quality before reports are finalized.
Assist project teams with monitoring commitments, planned and actual milestones, budget information, forecast inputs, invoice status, and other assigned performance indicators.
Elevate discrepancies, missing inputs, overdue actions, and emerging concerns to the appropriate project manager or portfolio lead.

Commercial and administrative coordination

Support contract administration, purchase-order tracking, subcontractor documentation, invoice workflows, and procurement coordination.
Assist with collecting and validating timesheet, expense, vendor, invoice, and cost-reporting information.
Maintain records supporting scope changes, extra-work requests, authorization status, and commercial decisions.
Coordinate required onboarding and offboarding activities, including system access, project documentation, distribution lists, credentials, and required training.

Safety, quality, and compliance

Job Details:

About Us

The University of Texas at Austin is one of the largest employers in the great city of Austin, offering thousands of career opportunities in a wide variety of fields. Deeply committed to recruiting and retaining a diverse and talented workforce, the university offers competitive salaries, full benefits, an extensive support network, and above all, an enriching and highly collaborative working community that is deeply passionate about our vision for higher education and public service.

General notes

This position is funded through June 30, 2030. Renewal of this position is based on renewal of funding, job performance, and department needs.

Purpose

To perform advanced research program administration and coordination for a multi-site NIH-funded study, including day-to-day project operations, participant recruitment, research staff supervision, regulatory coordination, data management, and collaboration with clinical and community partners.

Our research team, led by Dr. Jung Kwak, is conducting an NIH-funded study developing a framework to match transitional care services to the needs of persons living with dementia and their family caregivers, using longitudinal data collection, stakeholder interviews, and toolkit co-design across three Texas hospital sites. We are seeking a highly organized and detail-oriented project manager with strong experience recruiting research participants and managing research staff. The project manager will oversee day-to-day study operations at the UT Austin site, including IRB submissions and regulatory reporting, participant recruitment, staff supervision, and data management, and will serve as the primary point of coordination with the Baylor Houston site.

This role requires regular in-person coordination with hospital partners: the project manager will travel routinely to Dell Seton Medical Center Austin and Ascension Seton Medical Center Austin to support participant recruitment and maintain working relationships with clinical staff.

Responsibilities

Project Coordination and Site Management

Lead day-to-day project management and coordination for the study at the UT Austin site, working closely with the Baylor Houston site coordinator
Travel routinely to Dell Seton Medical Center Austin and Ascension Seton Medical Center Austin to support recruitment and coordinate with hospital staff
Serve as the primary liaison with hospital partners, skilled nursing facilities, and community organizations in the Austin area
Coordinate Community Advisory Board (CAB) activities, including member recruitment and quarterly meeting logistics

Recruitment and Staff Supervision

Oversee the recruitment process: identify, screen, recruit, and enroll hospitalized patients and family caregivers, and coordinate recruitment from skilled nursing facilities and community organizations in the Austin area
Coordinate participant follow-up and retention activities, including tracking completion of 1- and 3-month assessments
Supervise graduate research assistants at the Austin sites
Coordinate with the Baylor Houston site coordinator and support cross-site training and consistent implementation of study procedures

Regulatory and Data Management

Manage IRB applications, protocol amendments, and IRB/sponsor reporting requirements
Oversee data collection and manage data integrity across study databases (REDCap, Excel)
Prepare data, figures, and references to support manuscripts and presentations

Administrative and Budget Management

Track day-to-day project expenditures, purchasing, participant payments, and research supplies in coordination with the PI and School of Nursing post-award staff
Complete and maintain required research compliance training and certifications, including CITI and HIPAA training, for the duration of the award

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in a field related to the work to be performed and 3 years of responsible-level experience in program administration or coordination; OR Master's degree in a related field with at least 1 year of responsible-level experience
Research experience in psychology, healthcare, social work, nursing, or a related field
Demonstrated experience recruiting research participants
Working proficiency in spoken and written Spanish, sufficient to communicate directly with Spanish-speaking participants and family caregivers
Strong organizational skills with careful attention to detail and follow-through
Ability to manage multiple concurrent tasks, deadlines, and priorities
Strong verbal and written communication skills
Reliable transportation and ability to travel regularly between Austin sites

Relevant education and experience may be substituted as appropriate.

Preferred Qualifications

Master's degree in nursing, public health, social work, or a related field
Prior experience as a research coordinator or project manager recruiting participants in a clinical, hospital, or community-based health services study
Experience working with older adults, persons living with dementia, or family caregivers
Experience supervising research staff or student workers
Independent, self-motivated, and effective with limited supervision
Proactive, solution-oriented approach to problem-solving

$60,000 - $75,000 depending on qualifications

Working Conditions

Standard office environment; regular travel to hospital sites in Austin

The Program Coordinator II, in partnership with the residency program director, coordinates and manages the daily activities of the Psychiatry Residency at Texas A&M. Serves as a liaison to program administrators, residents, faculty, and associated staff of the School of Medicine. Responsibilities:

Program coordination, administration, and oversight

Coordinates and administers the psychiatry residency program, including creating and maintaining resident training files within various online repositories in accordance with the rules and standards established by the Accreditation Council for Graduate Medical Education (ACGME), the American Board of Psychiatry and Neurology (ABPN), Texas Medical Board (TMB), and other oversight bodies.
Oversees a coordinated system of faculty and resident scheduling to ensure achievement of educational objectives which complement the effective operation of a clinical enterprise while ensuring compliance with all applicable accreditation standards.
Implements a system of effective and efficient resident recruitment, interviewing, and onboarding.

Learning Management System Administration

Business processes, administrative management, and regulatory affairs

Assists GME leadership at Texas A&M with administrative responsibilities related to maintenance of all Affiliation Agreements between participating sites and the sponsoring institution, Program Letters of Agreement between programs and rotation sites, and other agreements as necessary.
Oversees processes relating to resident and faculty licensure, certifications, and other regulatory affairs as required by Texas A&M Health and affiliate teaching sites.
Coordinates, develops, evaluates, and ensures adherence to office procedures to eliminate duplication of effort and streamline flow of operations.

Accreditation Coordination

Maintains effective communication with community partners, affiliate health systems, and alumni.

Description

The Research Program Coordinator I develops and/or participates in study protocols, designs management and statistical plans, analyzes data and prepares final reports for human subjects research projects within the Neuro-Emergencies Management and Transfer (NEMAT) program.

Responsibilities

Provides assistance and consultation on clinical trials methodologies and statistical analysis issues.
Participates in the primary analysis of evaluation datasets.
Designs and implements research projects focusing on health, interventions, and their associated health outcomes.
Assists evaluation staff in project design, appropriate procedures, conduct, and coordination by establishing sample size requirements, calculating issues associated with various evaluation design options and consulting on appropriate statistical analysis for proposed evaluations.
Documents and records observations on progress of research, investigations and data per regulatory requirements and MSMC protocols.
Supervises subordinate personnel and offers guidance on research methods and techniques.
Provides assistance to the Principal Investigator or Research Manager on grant applications.
Assists in the development of budgets for research projects. Completes grant applications and proposals by developing pilot studies and generating pre-clinical data.
Completes and/or oversees Institutional Review Board (IRB) or IACUC submissions, and other regulatory applications and renewals as necessary.
Develops consent forms, screens and enrolls patients, follows patients through course of study. Collects and analyzes data.
Develops policies and procedures within area of responsibility. Writes and amends protocols as necessary.
Participates in conferences, meetings and seminars concerning research and surveillance projects.
Collaborates with Principal Investigator and other faculty/staff on research projects and papers to be published.
Oversees and/or maintains the NEMAT quality assurance database. Conducts regular audits for accuracy and completeness, and runs reports for quarterly QA/QI data presentations.
Performs other related duties.

Qualifications

Master’s degree in Natural Sciences OR Bachelor’s degree in Natural Sciences plus 5 years of progressive research experience with some experience in research administration preferred
4 years of research experience (5 years if no Master’s degree) in data management and study coordination in healthcare or basic research.
Bilingual in English/Spanish preferred

Employer Description

Strength through Unity and Inclusion

The Mount Sinai Health System is committed to fostering an environment where everyone can contribute to excellence. We share a common dedication to delivering outstanding patient care. When you join us, you become part of Mount Sinai’s unparalleled legacy of achievement, education, and innovation as we work together to transform healthcare. We encourage all team members to actively participate in creating a culture that ensures fair access to opportunities, promotes inclusive practices, and supports the success of every individual.

We are dedicated to building a supportive and welcoming environment where everyone has the opportunity to thrive and advance professionally. Explore this opportunity and be part of the next chapter in our history.

Mount Sinai Health System is one of the largest academic medical systems in the New York metro area, with more than 48,000 employees working across eight hospitals, more than 400 outpatient practices, more than 300 labs, a school of nursing, and a leading school of medicine and graduate education. Mount Sinai advances health for all people, everywhere, by taking on the most complex health care challenges of our time — discovering and applying new scientific learning and knowledge; developing safer, more effective treatments; educating the next generation of medical leaders and innovators; and supporting local communities by delivering high-quality care to all who need it. Through the integration of its hospitals, labs, and schools, Mount Sinai offers comprehensive health care solutions from birth through geriatrics, leveraging innovative approaches such as artificial intelligence and informatics while keeping patients’ medical and emotional needs at the center of all treatment. The Health System includes more than 9,000 primary and specialty care physicians; 13 joint-venture outpatient surgery centers throughout the five boroughs of New York City, Westchester, Long Island, and Florida; and more than 30 affiliated community health centers. We are consistently ranked by U.S. News & World Report's Best Hospitals, receiving high "Honor Roll" status, and are highly ranked: No. 1 in Geriatrics, top 5 in Cardiology/Heart Surgery, and top 20 in Diabetes/Endocrinology, Gastroenterology/GI Surgery, Neurology/Neurosurgery, Orthopedics, Pulmonology/Lung Surgery, Rehabilitation, and Urology. New York Eye and Ear Infirmary of Mount Sinai is ranked No. 12 in Ophthalmology. U.S. News & World Report’s “Best Children’s Hospitals” ranks Mount Sinai Kravis Children's Hospital among the country’s best in several pediatric specialties. The Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai is ranked No. 11 nationwide in National Institutes of Health funding and in the 99th percentile in research dollars per investigator according to the Association of American Medical Colleges. Newsweek’s “The World’s Best Smart Hospitals” ranks The Mount Sinai Hospital as No. 1 in New York and in the top five globally, and Mount Sinai Morningside in the top 20 globally.

Position: 
Program Coordinator, Collegiate Programs
Department: 
Pre-College and Collegiate Division (PCD)
Location:
New York

Senior Program Manager, Collegiate Programs
Classification: 
Permanent, Full Time

Immediate
Hours
: Approximately 40 hours per week during business hours 9am – 5pm, Monday – Friday; some 
evening and weekend work required; additional hours may be pre-approved by the Senior Program Manager during periods of high delivery demands.
Salary:
  $24 / hr.
Position Context 

Edconic is a successful group of education businesses, including Sotheby’s Institute of Art, The School of The New York Times, Manchester City Sports Business School, and Vogue College of Fashion. Its mission is to build compelling education programs in partnership with the world’s best brands. The Pre-College and Collegiate Division (PCD) supports its expansion and plans for growth by working across schools on the development and delivery of non-MA programs.
 The Program Coordinator, Collegiate Programs role is integral to the delivery of Collegiate Program within Sotheby’s Institute of Art – New York, Vogue College of Fashion – New York, and School of the New York Times. Sotheby’s Institute of Art, founded by Sotheby’s Auction House in 1969, has pioneered the education of arts professionals and offers a wide range of Masters’ degrees, semester courses, and professional programs. Since 2004, Vogue College of Fashion has been providing students with the knowledge, networks and practical experience to become future leaders in the fashion industry and offers a range of degree and non-degree programs. School of The New York Times, established in partnership with The New York Times in 2016, provides students with an immersive educational experience rooted in journalism, media, and storytelling. Drawing on the expertise and resources of The New York Times, the School offers a range of programs designed to develop practical skills, critical thinking, and industry knowledge for aspiring journalists, writers, and media professionals. Collegiate (undergraduate) academic courses are validated by the University of Montana.

Role Purpose

 The Program Coordinator plays an essential role in the preparation and successful delivery of Collegiate Programs. Reporting to the Senior Program Manager, this role supports the planning, developing, and execution of program delivery and contributing to the overall operations of Collegiate, ensuring a well-organized program. 
The role includes responsibilities such as coordinating co-curricular activities, onboarding faculty and guest speakers, handling class materials, overseeing logistics, and facilitating communication between staff, faculty, guest speakers and students. The Program Coordinator also supports student needs and assists with general operational tasks throughout the program. 
Serving as a primary point of contact for students and course leaders, the Program Coordinator will liaise with internal departments including facilities and IT. They will also work closely with colleagues to provide consistent, high-quality administrative support to both students and staff.
This is a full-time position that requires on-site support
during program delivery, or as directed by the Senior Program Manager. The role will include some evening and weekend hours, as well as additional duties as required with reasonable notice.
Essential Duties and Responsibilities

The Program Coordinator plays a vital role in supporting the planning and delivery of Collegiate programs, ensuring a high-quality and well-organized experience for students, faculty, and partners. Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:
Program Delivery & Operations:

 Support the coordination and execution of all on-the-ground program operations, including scheduling, catering, transportation, classroom logistics, and site visits. Ensure all activities run smoothly and efficiently.
Site Visits & Events Coordination:

Organize, book, and track logistics for site visits, co-curricular activities, and student events. Serve as a chaperone when needed. 
Classroom & Materials Management:

 Prepare and distribute class materials, supplies, and resources, ensuring all program-related materials are delivered accurately and on time.
Guest Speaker & Faculty Support:

Coordinate guest speaker logistics, including onboarding documentation, contracts, payments, scheduling, and technical setup (e.g., Zoom). 
Provide ongoing support to faculty and assist with faculty-related activities and events. Meet with faculty prior to the program to review course content, identify teaching support needs, and confirm classroom requirements.
Communication & Stakeholder Coordination:

 Act as a key point of contact for students, faculty, and course leaders. Manage program communications, including monitoring shared inboxes, and facilitating coordination with internal departments (Facilities and IT) and external vendors.
Student Support & Welfare:

 Provide day-to-day support to students, responding to inquiries and addressing concerns. Monitor student wellbeing and escalate issues as appropriate to senior staff. Contribute to a safe, inclusive, and supportive environment. 
Administrative & Financial Support:

 Maintain accurate records, track budgets, process invoices, and support financial reporting. Assist with purchasing tickets, supplies, and other program-related items.
Systems & Data Management:

 Maintain student-facing platforms (e.g., Canvas) with up-to-date schedules, course materials, and resources. Track and manage program data using internal systems. 
Program Activities & Engagement:

 Support in organizing and delivering virtual and in-person pre-program orientations, in-person orientation sessions, ongoing student engagement activities, and end-of-program events.
Continuous Improvement & Team Participation:

 Contribute to team meetings, planning sessions, and feedback collection processes. Support program evaluation and continuous improvement initiatives. 
On-Call & Flexibility:

 Participate in an emergency on-call rotation during program delivery and be available for occasional evening and weekend work as required.

Essential Skills and Experience

Proven administrative experience, ideally within an educational or student-focused environment 
Strong organizational and multitasking skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities 
Excellent verbal and written communication skills 
Ability to work both independently and collaboratively within a team 
High level of professionalism, discretion, and attention to detail 
Adaptability and problem-solving skills in fast-paced, dynamic environments 
Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint) 
Willingness to learn and use systems such as Canvas, Monday.com, DocuSign, and communication platforms
Student-centered approach with a commitment to fostering a safe, inclusive, and engaging environment 
Confidence navigating urban environments and supporting off-site activities if needed
Interest or experience working with college-age students (typically ages 18–22)
Education & Additional Requirements

Bachelor’s degree (or currently pursuing) or equivalent experience 
At least 2 years of relevant administrative or program support experience (education or university/college programs preferred)
Experience in residential life, student life, and/or student services preferred, including supporting students in a housing environment, campus organizations or clubs, and/or student services, as well as providing pastoral care and support to students or young people, with a focus on fostering a safe, inclusive, and community-oriented experience; ability to meet the physical demands of the role (e.g., standing, walking, lifting up to 25 lbs.)
Willingness to work on-site during key pre-program planning and throughout program delivery 
Availability during key program delivery periods, including occasional evenings and weekends.
Must be legally authorization to work in the US.
Work Environment

If working within a community setting with intellectually and developmentally disabled adults (over the age of 22) where YOU can make a difference sounds like a rewarding career, then consider a career with Devereux Advanced Behavioral Health!

The pay for this position starts at $23.54/hour, with additional compensation added for higher education and/or years of relevant experience up to $27.84/hour.

This position is located in Sterling, MA.

The schedule for this position is Monday to Friday 9:00am to 5:00pm.

$1,000 Sign-on Bonus

Additional $250 Bonus if MAP Certified

Devereux Advanced Behavioral Health – Massachusetts
is a nationally recognized organization dedicated to helping children and adults with Autism Spectrum Disorders and other psychological, emotional, and behavioral disorders. Through our residential and placement services in the community, we help individuals learn the skills needed for independent living and making meaningful life choices. We provide supportive settings in comfortable home environments and ensure that individuals have access to services that are appropriate to their developmental level, and cognitive, emotional, and social abilities.

As the Program Coordinator
, you will be responsible for the daily operations of a group home, including supervision of staff, management of program budget, and assurance of quality milieu services. You will also be responsible for ensuring that the group home is compliant with agency, state, and federal contracts and regulations, including all Medication Administration Protocols.

Being Program Coordinator at Devereux has its advantages
!

You will work with other dedicated professionals who share your passion for helping individuals in need. We offer you the privilege of being able to work closely with some of the most vulnerable people in our community, help build their strengths, and truly make a contribution to improving their lives. You will supervise staff, run shifts, and assist the Adult Services Director with development of programming for the house.

Responsibilities

About Manatee Memorial Hospital (MMH):

Manatee Memorial Hospital in Bradenton, Florida, has served the citizens of Manatee, Sarasota and surrounding counties for over 70 years. Part of the Manatee Healthcare System, the hospital has earned The Joint Commission’s Gold Seal of Approval. The 295-bed hospital with over 800 physicians, residents and allied health professionals, offers advanced healthcare services in a caring and compassionate environment. Services include cardiac care and cardiovascular medicine, emergency care for all ages, surgery services — including robotic-assisted surgery with the da Vinci® Surgical System, a weight-loss program, orthopedic services, outpatient and inpatient radiology and rehabilitation, respiratory care, sleep, oncology, wound care and women’s and children’s services. Manatee Memorial Hospital also offers a Level II Neonatal Intensive Care Unit for babies with special needs.

Position Summary:

The Pharmacy Residency Program Coordinator supports the administration and day-to-day operations of the Pharmacy Residency Program in collaboration with the Residency Program Director (RPD), Pharmacy Leadership, and Graduate Medical Education (GME). This role coordinates residency program activities, maintains program records and accreditation documentation, facilitates resident onboarding and educational activities, and supports recruitment, evaluation, and program compliance. This role will also serve the facility as the primary Internal Medicine pharmacist which entails regular interdisciplinary rounds, medication profile optimization, patient education and teaching all types of learners. The Pharmacy Residency Program Coordinator serves as a resource to residents, preceptors, pharmacy staff, and organizational departments regarding residency program requirements, schedules, and administrative processes. This role provides patient care support to the Internal Medicine team and serves as a preceptor to pharmacy students and residents. In addition, this role supports continuous program improvement and assists with activities necessary to maintain compliance with applicable accreditation and organizational standards. Demonstrates Service Excellence at all times. Other duties as assigned.

Position Information:

This position is for a full-time Pharmacy Residency Program Coordinator
Minimum of three (3) years acute care pharmacist experience

All UHS subsidiaries are committed to providing an environment of mutual respect where equal employment opportunities are available to all applicants and teammates. Avoid and Report Recruitment Scams

We are aware of a scam whereby imposters are posing as Recruiters from UHS, and our subsidiary hospitals and facilities. Beware of anyone requesting financial or personal information.

At UHS and all our subsidiaries, our Human Resources departments and recruiters are here to help prospective candidates by matching skill set and experience with the best possible career path at UHS and our subsidiaries. During the recruitment process, no recruiter or employee will request financial or personal information (e.g., Social Security Number, credit card or bank information, etc.) from you via email. Our recruiters will not email you from a public webmail client like Hotmail, Gmail, Yahoo Mail, etc. If you suspect a fraudulent job posting or job-related email mentioning UHS or its subsidiaries, we encourage you to report such concerns to appropriate law enforcement. We encourage you to refer to legitimate UHS and UHS subsidiary career websites to verify job opportunities and not rely on unsolicited calls from recruiters.
